Dr. Nguyen: Hi there, thanks for coming in. This is Miso, right? Our eleven-year-old domestic shorthair. Is this the annual exam?
Owner: Yes, he's due for his annual and his vaccines. I do have a concern, though. I think he's lost weight. His ribs feel more obvious than last year, and he's eating more than ever, always begging at the bowl.
Dr. Nguyen: Okay, good to know. Last visit he weighed 5.8 kilograms. How long have you noticed the change?
Owner: Maybe two or three months. He's also drinking more, I'm refilling the fountain almost daily. He has been a bit more vocal at night. No vomiting, no diarrhea that I've seen. He still uses the litter box, but the clumps are bigger.
Dr. Nguyen: Is he indoor only? Any changes at home, new pets, new food?
Owner: Indoor only, he lives with one other cat, Pepper, who is fine. Same dry food for years, plus a spoon of wet in the evening. No medications. He's up to date on flea prevention, I use the spot-on every month.
Dr. Nguyen: Thank you. Let's examine him. Today Miso weighs 4.9 kilograms, so he's down almost one kilogram, about fifteen percent. Temperature 101.8 Fahrenheit. Heart rate is fast at 220 beats per minute, respiratory rate 32 breaths per minute, no open mouth breathing. Body condition score is 4 out of 9. Mucous membranes pink, capillary refill less than two seconds.
Dr. Nguyen: On palpation I can feel a slightly enlarged thyroid nodule on the right side of the neck. His coat is a bit unkempt. I hear a soft grade two out of six systolic murmur that I didn't hear last year. Abdomen is soft, kidneys feel normal in size. Mild tartar and gingivitis on the upper premolars, no painful areas.
Owner: What do you think it is?
Dr. Nguyen: With the weight loss, increased appetite, thirst, fast heart rate and that thyroid nodule, I'm suspicious of hyperthyroidism. Kidney disease and diabetes are also on the list, so I recommend a full senior blood panel with a total T4, a urinalysis, and a blood pressure measurement today. We should also consider an echocardiogram because of the new murmur, since hyperthyroidism can affect the heart.
Owner: Yes, let's do the bloodwork. And the vaccines?
Dr. Nguyen: I'll give his FVRCP booster today since he's indoor only, and his rabies vaccine is current until next year, so we'll skip that today. I'd like to hold off on any other vaccine until we know the bloodwork. We will call you with the results tomorrow, and if the T4 is high we'll discuss treatment options, like tablets or a prescription diet. Please keep an eye on his water intake and weight, and recheck blood pressure in two weeks.
Owner: Okay, thank you. Please call me as soon as you have the results.
